section: For the founder: What it means
claim: At launch each way to pay leaves the money where its own arrangement puts it (wallet or bank: the seller's own account; courier: until it settles; bank transfer or cash to staff: the seller); Sharrwah holds none and bills its fees separately
evidence: SA-en:234 "cash on delivery amounts are transferred to the merchant every 5 business days"; SA-en:277 "If there are cash on delivery amounts held for you, the invoice total is deducted from them."; SA-en:565 "Bank transfer (customers transfer payment directly to your account)", "Cash on Delivery (collected by the shipping company or your own courier)"; decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:195 Cash Pay "added to your Cash Wallet account"
note: Holds on the held cases. Its "seller's own account" inherits C09 and C10. "Bills its own fees separately" is D-004 row 9's answer, which this page says confirming also settles (D-001:47).

section: For the founder: The line's words (held through Sharrwah)
claim: B is "a payment company holds it in an account opened through Sharrwah, the way Shopify Payments is set up inside Shopify"; "A seller linking its own account with a provider, by its own keys, is neither."
evidence: founder-decisions.tsv:9, the guard's B: "a payment company holds it in an account opened through Sharrwah (option B)"; SA-en:576 "To request a new Tabby Business account through Salla"; SA-ar:880 "اختر (إرسال طلب فتح حساب أعمال)", "راجع المعلومات التي سيشاركها متجرك مع تابي"; SA-en:29 "the Tabby team emails you your account details ... Enter the Merchant Key for your Tabby account"; SA-ar:865 "تُحصّل المدفوعات التي تتم عبر تابي من خلال تابي وليس من خلال مدفوعات سلة"; SA-en:577 and SA-ar:881 the same for Tamara ("إنشاء حساب أعمال جديد على تمارا وتفعيله"); HC:payments/paypal/set-up-paypal.md:3 "a PayPal Express Checkout account is automatically generated using the email address that you use to sign in. This account allows you to receive payments from PayPal orders."
proposed_wording: Held through Sharrwah: A, Sharrwah holds it, as Salla presents the balance of its electronic payments; or B, a payment company holds it in an account opened through Sharrwah: with Sharrwah's own payment service, the way Shopify Payments is set up inside Shopify, or with a provider whose account Sharrwah requests or creates for the seller, as Salla does for Tabby and Shopify for PayPal. A seller linking an account it opened with a provider itself, by its own keys, is neither. A case between them comes to you before it goes live.
note: interpretation: by the guard's plain words, a Tabby or Tamara business account requested through Salla, and the PayPal account Shopify generates at sign-up, are accounts opened through the platform in which a payment company holds the money: B. The page's last sentence puts the Tabby case on neither side, since the seller links it by its own Merchant Key. Confirming the line as worded would settle, unseen, a case the guard reserves to the founder.

section: For the founder: The line's words (at launch)
claim: At launch: from the day Sharrwah first goes live, for as long as you haven't switched A or B on.
evidence: decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:40 (founder's text) against :68 (Terms) "From first going live in any market, for as long as the founder hasn't switched A or B on there"; architecture/12-glossary.md:48 "for as long as the founder hasn't switched A or B on there"; D-001:83 "Only the founder switches either on, in a market"

note: The record relies on a per-market extent (D-001:68, :83) that the founder's text (D-001:40) lacks. interpretation: on the founder's text, switching B on in one market would end "at launch" in all of them.

section: For the founder: The line's words (reserved, not built); Terms: reserved, not built

proposed_wording: Reserved, not built: nothing of A or B is designed, built, integrated or contracted.

note: Holds on both platforms' held cases. Its first clause inherits C09 and C10; its last sentence inherits C19 (who decides that A or B is built).

claim: C. Each payment method's provider holds it, in the seller's own account with that provider; needs "an integration with each provider"; from outside, "a contract between the seller and each provider"
evidence: decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:121 (the row) against :128-129 (the outcome puts under C a courier, "until it settles with the seller", and a manual method, "with the seller"); SA-en:277 COD "amounts held for you" by the carrier; SA-en:565 bank transfer "directly to your account"
proposed_wording: C. Each payment method's own arrangement holds it: a provider, in the seller's own account with it; a courier under the seller's own contract, until it settles with the seller; the seller, for a manual method ... "an integration with each provider and courier (none for a manual method), and one boundary over them (D-002)" ... "a contract between the seller and each provider or courier"
note: The row covers only the first of the outcome's three cases. A courier holds the cash itself (SA-en:277), not in an account of the seller's.

claim: The seller's account with a provider or courier under its own contract, linked by its own credentials, keys or account number: option C
evidence: SA-en:9 "The bank account in the Store Verification page: It is used to transfer your dues from Salla to your bank account"; GQL:3229 "The interval at which payouts are sent to the connected bank account."; SA-en:793 PayPal on Salla: "the email address for your PayPal account in the field provided"
proposed_wording: An account the seller opened with a provider or courier itself, under its own contract, into which that provider or courier receives or settles the buyer's payment, linked to Sharrwah by the seller's own credentials, keys or account identifier: option C. A bank account that only receives payouts from a platform balance, or from an account opened through Sharrwah, is not C.
note: interpretation: as written, the payout account of every A and B arrangement meets the definition: Salla's verification bank account (A, SA-en:9) and Shopify Payments' connected bank account (B, GQL:3229) are the seller's own accounts with its bank, linked by account number. Salla links PayPal by the account's email (SA-en:793), which "credentials, keys or account number" doesn't name.

section: Terms: held through Sharrwah (the line between B and C)
claim: Glossary: B is "one the seller sets up from inside the platform, with the platform's own payment service"; C "one the seller holds with a provider under its own contract, and links to the platform"; "Both platforms draw this line"; "Nothing else is held through Sharrwah"
evidence: founder-decisions.tsv:9, the guard's B: "a payment company holds it in an account opened through Sharrwah", not limited to the platform's own service; architecture/12-glossary.md:34-35; SA-en:576 and SA-ar:880 a Tabby business account requested through Salla (Saudi stores only: "حالياً للمتاجر في المملكة العربية السعودية فقط"); SA-en:29 Merchant Key; SA-ar:865 "للاتفاقية المبرمة بينك وبين تابي"; SA-en:577 and SA-ar:881 Tamara; HC:payments/paypal.md:5 "Shopify asks for your email to set up this account, which is then shared with PayPal"; HC:payments/paypal/set-up-paypal.md:3 "This account allows you to receive payments from PayPal orders."; :20 "the payment was sent to an unverified PayPal account"; HC:payments/paypal/common-issues.md:33 "Log in to your PayPal account to grant Shopify the required access"
proposed_wording: Glossary, Here: "An account opened through Sharrwah (B) is one the seller did not open with the provider itself: with the platform's own payment service, or with a provider from which the platform requests or creates the account for the seller. The seller's own account (C) is one the seller opened with the provider itself, under its own contract, and links to the platform. Both platforms show both, and cases between them (Salla's request for a Tabby business account, SA-ar:880; Shopify's generated PayPal account, HC:payments/paypal/set-up-paypal.md:3). Such a case goes to the founder before it goes live."
note: The definition (glossary:35) narrows the guard (founder-decisions.tsv:9) to the platform's own service. interpretation: the Tabby or Tamara account requested through Salla is C by the definition (own agreement, own Merchant Key) and B by the guard's words. The PayPal account Shopify generates at sign-up receives payments before the seller links anything (set-up-paypal.md:3), so it is neither B as defined nor C, and "Nothing else" puts it outside the guard. The glossary's Open note (glossary:38) covers onboarding "the seller would start"; the PayPal case is started by the platform.

claim: What a buyer pays for a seller's order, until the seller has it
evidence: HC:finance/shopify-balance/payouts.md:3 "receive Shopify Payments earnings in your main Shopify Balance account"; HC:finance/shopify-balance.md:3 "Shopify Balance is a money management account"; decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:95 "a business account receiving payouts through Sharrwah, is B"; D-001:84 "no account that would hold sellers' money through Sharrwah (part of area A-13)"
proposed_wording: What a buyer pays for a seller's order, until it reaches an account the seller holds outside Sharrwah: its own account with a provider, or its own bank account. Money paid out into an account opened through Sharrwah is still sellers' money.
note: Until the seller has it (glossary:22; D-001:65) doesn't say whether payouts into a business account opened through the platform, such as Shopify Balance, are still sellers' money. interpretation: the Scope's B class for such an account (D-001:84, :95) needs them to be; the proposed wording states that reading.

claim: From first going live in any market, for as long as the founder hasn't switched A or B on there
evidence: decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:68; architecture/12-glossary.md:48-49 (its reading is marked as an interpretation)
note: The Terms extent is per market; the founder's text isn't (C03).

section: Terms: payment method (kind 2) and manual payment method
claim: paid to the seller directly and recorded by hand; "The buyer pays the seller directly, and the seller records it"
evidence: HC:payments/manual-payments.md:5 "Common types of manual payments include cash on delivery (COD), money orders, and bank transfers."; SA-en:565 "Cash on Delivery (collected by the shipping company or your own courier)"; SA-en:277 COD "amounts held for you"; architecture/12-glossary.md:114 "The money goes to the seller directly" against :120 "the courier holds the cash until it settles with the seller"
proposed_wording: D-001 Terms: "The buyer pays outside any provider integration, to the seller directly or, for cash on delivery, to a courier that settles with the seller; the seller records it." Glossary, manual payment method: "The money goes to the seller directly or, for cash on delivery through a courier, to the courier (cash on delivery)." Kind 2: "paid outside a provider, to the seller or its courier, and recorded by hand".
note: Both platforms count courier-collected COD as a manual method (HC manual-payments.md:5; SA-en:565), though the buyer pays the courier, not the seller. The glossary's two entries (:114, :120) disagree on where the money goes.

claim: The company that processes or receives a payment for a method; glossary: "D-001 names a courier collecting cash on delivery apart from providers"
evidence: architecture/12-glossary.md:107; decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:71; decisions/D-004-what-follows-from-decision-1.md:75, row 4: "each provider: the wallet, the courier, or the seller's own bank account"; SA-en:234 a carrier transfers COD amounts "to the merchant"
proposed_wording: In both Terms tables and the glossary: "The company that processes or receives a payment for a method, a platform's own service included. A courier collecting cash on delivery is named apart; where a record means both it says 'provider or courier'." Then D-004 row 4: "each provider or courier: the wallet, the courier, or the seller's own bank".
note: interpretation: a courier "receives a payment for a method" (COD), so the definition takes it in. The glossary says D-001 names it apart (glossary:107), and D-004 row 4 counts it as a provider (D-004:75): three texts, three extents. Row 4 also names "the seller's own bank account" as a provider; the provider is the bank.

claim: Cash to a courier or to the seller's own staff; a courier under the seller's own contract holds it until it settles; cash collected into a platform balance is A
evidence: SA-en:565; SA-en:234; SA-ar:602 "ويتم تحويل مبالغ الدفع عند الاستلام كل 5 أيام عمل للتاجر"; SA-en:277 and SA-ar:359 "يتم خصم مبلغ الفاتورة منها"; SA-en:570 "The transfer days for cash on delivery balances from shipping companies that support COD via Salla shipping labels"
note: Holds for both held arrangements. D-004 relies only on the courier case. A courier under Sharrwah's own contract that settles with the seller directly fits neither sentence (C26).

claim: A balance of a platform's own payment service: A or B
evidence: SA-en:1240 "three main balances: Store balance, Electronic payments balance, Cash on Delivery (COD) payments balance"; SA-en:570 COD balances "from shipping companies that support COD via Salla shipping labels"; decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:73 "Cash collected into a platform balance is A"
proposed_wording: A balance a platform keeps for a seller, from its own payment service or from cash on delivery its own shipping labels collect: A or B.
note: Salla's COD balance is fed by its shipping labels (SA-en:570), not its payment service. interpretation: the definition leaves out a balance that the record's cash-on-delivery term calls A.

note: Both platforms bill their fees on sales they don't process. Salla also lets the electronic payments balance be moved into the store balance that pays for platform services (SA-en:1240), which needs a balance (A), off at launch.

section: Scope: Decides (bullets 1 and 3); Terms: reserved, not built
claim: neither A nor B is built (C at launch); "Only the founder switches either on, in a market, after it is built"
evidence: decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:81, :83; D-001:68, at launch lasts "for as long as the founder hasn't switched A or B on there"; architecture/12-glossary.md:53, switching on "can come only after the arrangement is built"; founder-decisions.tsv:9, the guard "limits only what goes live, and neither requires a proposal to provide for either arrangement nor rules one out"; D-001:212 (Review)
proposed_wording: A and B stay possible behind the payment boundary. Building either is a change to this record (Review), by the founder's decision; switching either on in a market is the founder's decision too.
note: interpretation: at launch lasts until A or B is switched on; switching on needs it built; and while at launch lasts, neither is built. The record doesn't say who decides that A or B is built, and as written that can happen only by changing this record. The Review line (D-001:212) points there; Decides should say so.

proposed_wording: Carried: under C any provider fits whose account the seller opened with it itself and links by its own keys. One whose account is opened through Sharrwah, by Sharrwah's own service or by a request Sharrwah makes for the seller, comes to the founder.

The outcome S-07 could reach: a provider whose merchant account the seller requests from inside Sharrwah under its own contract (as Salla's Tabby and Tamara), or one Sharrwah creates at sign-up (as Shopify's PayPal). interpretation: if S-07 classes it C under the record's definitions, it goes live without the founder though the guard's words call it B; if B, the record's C definition must change. Either way this record changes.

section: Scope: Leaves open (S-05, shipping with cash on delivery)

evidence: SA-en:570 (Salla's labels: COD into Salla's balance); SA-en:234, SA-en:277 (the seller's own contract: the carrier settles); decisions/D-001-who-holds-sellers-money.md:161 Zid Ship "تقوم زد بتحصيل المبالغ من العملاء النهائيين وتحويل إجمالي المستحقات إلى محفظة التاجر"; architecture/12-glossary.md:121 (Shopify: no collection by Shopify itself)
note: interpretation: S-05 could propose Sharrwah shipping labels under Sharrwah's contract with a courier that settles COD with each seller directly. That is neither C (not the seller's own contract), nor A (no Sharrwah balance), nor B as defined (no payment company's account), and "Nothing else" puts it outside the guard. No held case shows it: Salla's and Zid's labels collect into the platform's balance (assumption: no other held platform label arrangement was searched). What would settle it: S-05's proposal, or this record saying how a courier under Sharrwah's contract is classed.

The business account part rests on C11.

proposed_wording: A marketplace Sharrwah runs, collecting buyers' payments for sellers, would be A or B, which stay off. An outside marketplace where the seller sells under its own account and contract keeps the money under that contract, as C, or comes to the founder if its account is opened through Sharrwah.
